{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of sensitivity (88.7%) and specificity (88.9%) for predicting drug-induced liver injury (DILI) using their organoid model compared to known DILI compounds, which is a measure of agreement between the model and human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study focuses on drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and evaluates toxicity, including cholestatic and mitochondrial toxicity, making it a toxicology study.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study explicitly focuses on drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and uses human liver organoids (HLOs).",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses human pluripotent stem cell-derived liver organoids (HLOs) and evaluates their predictive capacity for drug-induced liver injury, which is a model system for toxicology.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study uses human pluripotent stem cells and human liver organoids, and compares their performance to human clinical outcomes. No other animal species are analyzed or used as models.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses multiple readouts including viability, cholestatic function (CLF transport inhibition), and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), which are a mix of biomarker and functional outcome measures."
}
